quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: Motorcycles do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
Motorcycles brake more slowly than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles can stop much faster than regular vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop quickly. Following too closely puts you and the motorcyclist in danger. You need enough distance to avoid a crash if the motorcyclist stops suddenly.

questions.question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns about road conditions ahead.
It helps you find cities and towns ahead.
It tells you about traffic laws.
It tells you about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns about road conditions ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols on a yellow background. They tell you about dangerous conditions on or near the road.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for other traffic, and go through carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge.
Winding road ahead.
Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic will soon become one lane.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Driver error
Bad weather
Poor road conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: Driver error
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when drivers don't see other vehicles or make unexpected moves. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: When should you be most careful when turning or stopping in rain?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
Half an hour after the rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed away and mixes with rain to create a slippery surface.

questions.question: When must you stop at an intersection?

options.text: When you see a flashing red light.
When you see a steady yellow light.
When you see a yellow arrow.
When you see a flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow center line. What does this tell you?

options.text: You are on a two-way road.
You are on a one-way road.
The road is under repair.
You must stay to the left of the line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a two-way road.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A broken line means you can pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use the side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot see all areas around your vehicle. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check blind spots that mirrors cannot see.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Be ready for traffic merging into your lane.
Always stop.
Divided highway ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for traffic merging into your lane.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic will merge from the right, so be ready to let them in safely.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching you on a one-way street. What must you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, drive to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: Your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system. What should you do?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. If your vehicle has an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: You exit a freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. What should you do?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because oncoming traffic is unlikely.
By using the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass in a curve or on a hill because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Do not pass by driving on the shoulder. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to get ready.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you arrive at the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before the turn. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another vehicle hits you from behind.

questions.question: You need to slow down on a slippery road. What should you do first?

options.text: Firmly apply your brakes.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Apply your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently and slowly press the brake pedal.

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of moving traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and match the speed of moving traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal and enter at the same speed as traffic. Always yield to other drivers when entering a roadway.

questions.question: If you cannot merge safely into traffic, yielding also means you should stop.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When you must yield, you must also stop if you cannot merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the road.
Flaggers at construction sites.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flaggers at construction sites.
questions.explanation: You must obey flaggers at construction sites. They are there to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: If a train is close enough or fast enough to be dangerous, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down and proceed carefully.
Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find another route across the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is near enough or fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or the signals are not working.

questions.question: How can you prevent alcohol-related car crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Tell others no thanks if they offer you a drink while you are driving.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: Can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, when the train has passed.
No, never.
Yes, when the lights stop flashing.
Yes, if other drivers do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a flagger, or a train's horn. Never try to drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What happens if you drive slower than the flow of traffic?

options.text: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
You will improve traffic flow.
You will show good defensive driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will block traffic and may get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. However, if you drive too slowly and block normal traffic flow, you may get a ticket. Match the speed of traffic, unless traffic exceeds the legal speed limit.
